section_summary: This section begins with a Commerce Department request for reports on a collision involving the American steamship Michigan. It then follows the grounding, salvage, and repair plans for the Japanese Arima Maru in Peru, and diplomatic exchanges after the Kehi Maru struck a mine in the Sea of Japan. The final documents concern the sinking of the Lisbon Maru, prisoners of war who may have been aboard, and Japanese ship salvage and construction.

subfiles.title: Request for despatches on the Michigan–Koshi Maru collision
subfiles.about: Commerce requests two Tsingtao consular despatches for an investigation of the Michigan–Koshi Maru collision.
subfiles.summary: Requests copies of despatches 357 and 366 for the Bureau of Marine Inspection and Navigation.

subfiles.title: Despatch 1221 on the stranded Arima Maru
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, for the Ambassador, Lima
subfiles.about: The embassy forwards a consular agent’s report on the Japanese steamer stranded at Mollendo.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Ferrer’s letter and gives the Arima Maru’s tonnage and Tokyo home port.

subfiles.title: Ferrer’s account of the Arima Maru grounding
subfiles.about: Ferrer describes the ship’s position, cargo, damage, and limited assistance after it grounded near Mollendo.
subfiles.summary: Reports the vessel ashore with ore aboard, damaged engines, and its crew still on board.

subfiles.title: Despatch 1578 on proposed Arima Maru salvage
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, for the Ambassador, Lima
subfiles.about: The embassy forwards an update on the owners’ plans to salvage the Arima Maru.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Ferrer’s August report and notes that the owners intend to attempt salvage.

subfiles.title: Ferrer’s report on salvage preparations
subfiles.about: Japanese engineers and equipment have arrived to prepare the grounded Arima Maru to pull itself free.
subfiles.summary: Describes salvage materials, anchors, cargo discharge, and possible assistance from the Sakito Maru.

subfiles.title: Despatch 1783 on Arima Maru salvage progress
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, for the Ambassador, Lima
subfiles.about: The embassy forwards news of salvage progress and plans to dry-dock the Arima Maru at Callao.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Ferrer’s report and highlights the proposed move to Callao for repairs.

subfiles.title: Ferrer’s report that the Arima Maru is afloat
subfiles.about: The Arima Maru has been refloated and is being prepared for a tow to Callao.
subfiles.summary: Reports hull repairs, water in two holds, cargo jettisoning, and a planned tow by the Sakito Maru.

subfiles.title: State Department routing sheet
subfiles.about: An administrative sheet records State Department handling of the preceding material.
subfiles.summary: Division names and routing marks only.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase reporting the Arima Maru afloat
subfiles.about: A brief paraphrase reports successful refloating near Mollendo.
subfiles.summary: Reports the Arima Maru afloat after salvage operations.

subfiles.title: Despatch 1887 on Arima Maru repairs
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, for the Ambassador, Lima
subfiles.about: The embassy reports the Arima Maru’s tow to Callao and obstacles to dry-docking it there.
subfiles.summary: Japanese personnel refloated the ship, and the Sakito Maru towed it to Callao. A local shop was contracted for minor plate repairs, but dry-dock space was unavailable for months; towing the ship to Kobe was being considered.

subfiles.title: Naval intelligence report on Arima Maru salvage
subfiles.about: The report describes how the Arima Maru pulled itself off the beach and discusses limits on dry-dock access.
subfiles.summary: Reports that the ship used anchors and its own winches after discharging cargo. Peruvian vessels had priority for the Callao dry dock.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1758 on the Kehi Maru mine disaster
subfiles.about: A Tokyo telegram relays reports that the passenger ship Kehi Maru struck a mine.
subfiles.summary: Reports the ship’s passenger and crew numbers, rescue efforts, and Japanese press claims that Soviet mines drifting from Vladivostok caused this and earlier incidents.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1767 on Japanese press reaction to the Kehi Maru sinking
subfiles.about: The telegram relays a newspaper editorial blaming Soviet mine laying for danger to shipping.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes a Nichi Nichi editorial assigning Soviet responsibility and criticizing drifting mines.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1763 on Japan’s protest over the Kehi Maru
subfiles.about: Japan has lodged a formal protest with the Soviet ambassador over the Kehi Maru sinking.
subfiles.summary: Reports the protest and spokesman Ishii’s statements about continuing danger from mines and the effect on Soviet-Japanese relations.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1804 on the Soviet reply to Japan
subfiles.about: A Soviet embassy source describes Moscow’s rejection of responsibility for the Kehi Maru sinking.
subfiles.summary: The Soviet reply disputes proof that its mine caused the sinking, says its mines become harmless if adrift, and raises the possibility of third-country involvement.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1826 on Japan’s renewed indemnity demand
subfiles.about: Japan rejects the Soviet answer and renews its demand for compensation and preventive action.
subfiles.summary: Reports a demand for indemnity for damage and deaths from the Kehi Maru sinking.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on Japan’s shipping shortage
subfiles.about: The note points to a telegram citing the Turkish ambassador in Tokyo on Japan’s shipping shortage.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a report that Japan was already short of shipping.

subfiles.title: Navy reply concerning the Lisbon Maru
subfiles.about: The Navy answers a request for information about casualties and possible public comment on the Lisbon Maru sinking.
subfiles.summary: Reports an earlier Japanese broadcast, no further casualty information, and no planned press statement.

subfiles.title: Saugstad memorandum forwarding Canadian inquiry
subfiles.about: Saugstad forwards a Canadian Legation inquiry on the Lisbon Maru to the Navy.
subfiles.summary: Requests the Navy’s views on an enclosed Canadian teletype.

subfiles.title: Canadian teletype on the Lisbon Maru and prisoners of war
subfiles.from: Secretary of State for External Affairs, Canada
subfiles.to: Canadian Minister to the United States
subfiles.about: Canada seeks evidence of whether Canadian prisoners were aboard the sunk Lisbon Maru and asks about a U.S. press statement.
subfiles.summary: Reports suggest that the ship carried British and American prisoners, possibly including men from North Point camp in Hong Kong. The sender requests route information to help establish who was aboard and asks whether U.S. authorities will address the sinking publicly.

subfiles.title: Clipping on escaped British naval officers
subfiles.about: A report describes three British officers who escaped from a torpedoed Japanese transport and reached Chinese-held territory.
subfiles.summary: Names Wallace Evans Johnston and recounts the officers’ escape and statements about conditions in a Hong Kong prisoner camp.

subfiles.title: State Department memorandum on the Lisbon Maru
subfiles.about: The memorandum records the Navy’s response to the Canadian inquiry about the Lisbon Maru.
subfiles.summary: Repeats that the Navy has no casualty information beyond a Japanese broadcast and does not plan a press statement.

subfiles.title: Hoover letter on Japanese salvage and shipbuilding
subfiles.about: Hoover relays an intercepted January 1943 message about Japanese efforts to salvage ships and build new ones.
subfiles.summary: Reports salvage work in Malaya and Sumatra, wooden ship construction in Java, seamen’s training, and shipyard activity in Hong Kong.
